data.name: Sharav
data.gender_notes: Sharav is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'shara' meaning 'king' and 'van' meaning 'forest', Sharav translates to 'brave in the forest'. The name Sharav carries the meaning “Brave” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharav usually hope their child will grow to embody brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sharav is a divine name that represents the courage and strength of Lord Shiva. It signifies victory over inner and outer challenges and is a reminder of the power within us.
data.etymology: Sharav belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharav total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sharav may evoke images of ancient Hindu warriors, who would bravely lead their armies through dense forests, facing nature's challenges and dangerous enemies. It could also symbolize royalty, with the connotation of a fearless monarch who protects his people and territory with unyielding courage. This name embodies great strength and bravery, encouraging those who bear it to manifest that same resilience in everyday life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Sharav represents the inner warrior within each of us, the part of our being that bravely faces challenges, overcoming fear and obstacles on our spiritual journey toward enlightenment. The name speaks to the valiant souls who continue on their path, fearlessly and unwavering, in the face of hardships. Through journeys and challenges, we gain wisdom and develop our inner strength, becoming the brave kings and queens of our own lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sharav: The radiant, invincible one, who triumphs over all difficulties, illuminating the path towards wisdom and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Sharav was a celebrated poet during the Gupta Empire in the 5th-6th century AD and is best known for his work 'Shatakarni Prabandha'. This work presents the story of a king and his attempts to gain immortality through various means including asecticism, sacrificial rituals and even poison.
historical_references.context: Gupta Empire, India, Poet, Literature, 'Shatakarni Prabandha'

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sharav is in the 'Harshacharita' of Banabhatta, where he is mentioned as a renowned scholar and a guru to King Harshavardhana in the 7th century AD. He was known for his knowledge of the Vedas, Puranas, and other Hindu scriptures and was respected for his spiritual wisdom.
historical_references.context: Harshavardhana, India, Scholar, Guru, Hindu scriptures, Spiritual wisdom

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
